content: Brendan Carvalho, an expert in obstetric anesthesia, contributed to the guideline development as both a content expert and end user. He co-authored one study included in the evidence synthesis. Additionally, he served as a paid consultant for Gauss Surgical, a company that developed artificial intelligence-informed gravimetric products for measuring blood loss. However, this declared conflict of interest was deemed insignificant and did not pose any risk to the guideline development process or its credibility. Rajat Khosla, a human rights expert, declared no conflicts of interest, and his contributions were not applicable to any potential conflicts. Tippawan Liabsuetrakul, an expert in obstetrics, declared no conflicts of interest, and no applicable management of declared interests was required. Elliott Kingwill Main, an expert in obstetrics, consulted on the development of perinatal quality improvement collaboratives aimed at implementing national safety bundles in the United States. His contract for this work ended on August 31, 2023. This declared conflict of interest was considered insignificant and did not pose any risk to the guideline development process or its credibility. Hadil Ali-Masri, an expert in obstetrics, declared no conflicts of interest, and no applicable management of declared interests was required. Martin Meremikwu, an expert in neonatology, declared no conflicts of interest, and no applicable management of declared interests was required. Kui Muraya, an expert in gender, social determinants, and equity, declared no conflicts of interest, and no applicable management of declared interests was required. Mari Nagai, an expert in health systems, declared no conflicts of interest, and no applicable management of declared interests was required. Angela Ndunge Nguku, representing community and stakeholder perspectives, declared no conflicts of interest, and no applicable management of declared interests was required. Aris Papageorghiou, the GDG Chair and an expert in obstetrics, is a practicing clinician who uses the medications and interventions included in the guideline in his clinical practice. This declared conflict of interest was considered insignificant and did not pose any risk to the guideline development process or its credibility. Dilys Walker, an expert in obstetrics, received a Saving Lives at Birth grant, through which she acts as a virtual mentor for a chatbot on postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) management. She is the co-founder of PRONTO and holds a patent for PartoPants, a simulation training tool. She also delivered a lecture on heat-stable carbetocin at a FIGO conference side event sponsored by Ferring Pharmaceuticals. Additionally, she was funded by the Gates Foundation to conduct a scoping review on sponge and suction tools for PPH. Despite these declared conflicts of interest, they were deemed insignificant and did not pose any risk to the guideline development process or its credibility.
